title: EFFINGHAM TORNADO
full_story:
Multiple injuries were reported and multiple structures were damaged following a tornado that struck areas north of Effingham last night.

The Effingham County Emergency Management Agency said a tornado caused extensive damage to homes, businesses, and farms in parts of the county.  “An impactful tornado traveled an estimated 12-to-15 miles through the northern part of Effingham County,” the agency said in a Facebook post early this morning.

Effingham Fire Chief, Brant Yochum, said crews responded to “numerous storm-related” emergencies, mainly in the Shumway and Siegel areas.  This included reports of heavily damaged homes, collapsed structures, motor vehicle crashes, downed power lines, gas leaks, blocked roadways, and more.  Yochum said several people had minor injuries within the Effingham Fire Department’s response area.  But none of those injuries were life-threatening.

Early this morning Effingham County Board Chair Josh Douthit announced a disaster declaration for the county.  He said the declaration frees up and expedites resources to parts of the county impacted by the tornado.  “At a time when many residents and first responders need support and resources Effingham County will be able to assist when and where appropriate and cooperate with local, state, and federal agencies to continue the recovery and restoration efforts needed for all of our residents,” Douthit said.

Effingham County Sheriff Paul Kuhns is discouraging people from driving around to look at damage.  Some roads are not passable, but congested areas creates issues for first responders trying to get to people who might need help.

title: IECC BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The Board of Trustees of the Illinois Eastern Community College District met Tuesday night at Olney Central College.

Jim Reed, representing the Illinois Community College Trustees Association (ICCTA), presented Dr. Ryan Gower with the recognition for his leadership and dedicated service to Illinois Eastern Community Colleges.  The Board of Trustees also recognized Dr. Gower for his ten years of service to Illinois Eastern Community Colleges, including his roles as President of Lincoln Trail College and Chancellor.  Trustees expressed their sincere appreciation for his commitment to student success, employees, and the communities served by IECC, and extended their best wishes to Dr. Gower.

The Board approved the purchase of a new video display system for the Frontier Community College Athletic Facility currently under construction.  The project, funded through a partnership with the FCC Foundation, includes a large video board, digital scorer’s table, shot clocks, locker room game clocks, and related installation and technical support provided by Watchfire of Danville, Illinois.

Beginning in Fall 2026, the Automotive Technology Associate in Applied Science program will relocate from Frontier Community College to Olney Central College.  As part of this transition, the Board approved the purchase of required equipment through the OCC Bookstore for the program, necessitating the addition of a cost recovery fee to the academic catalog.  The fee will be assessed at the actual cost of the equipment, ensuring students have access to the tools needed for the program while reflecting a change in the method of purchase rather than a new program requirement.

Changes in status were approved for Dr. Cathy Robb as Interim IECC Chancellor effective July 1st, to August 14th; Ryan Hawkins from Chief Financial Officer to Vice Chancellor of Financial Operations & OCC President-Delegate effective July 1st to May 17th, 2027; and Jamie Carman from Director of Academic Advising to Director of Advising Systems effective June 22nd.

Retirement ratifications were approved for Dr. Ryan Gower as IECC Chancellor effective June 30th, and Chris Simpson as OCC President & Vice Chancellor of Business Operations effective May 17th, 2027.

The Board approved contracts for Dr. Timothy Taylor, Chancellor effective August 15th, and Ryan Hawkins, Vice Chancellor of Financial Operations & OCC President effective May 18th, 2027.

The next regular meeting of the Board of Trustees will be Tuesday, July 21st, at 6:15 pm at Wabash Valley College, Mt. Carmel.

title: FREE FISHING DAYS
full_story:
Illinois Free Fishing Days start tomorrow and run through Monday, and the Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) invites families throughout the state to enjoy the opportunity at a lake, pond, river, state park or private fishing hole near them.

During these four days, anglers can fish without purchasing a fishing license, salmon stamp or inland trout stamp in Illinois.  The goal is for those who don’t usually go fishing to discover or rediscover the activity and to introduce children to it.

“Free Fishing Days are a great opportunity for Illinois families to unplug, spend time together outdoors, and discover the fun and enjoyment of fishing,” said IDNR Director Natalie Phelps Finnie.  “Whether you’re new to the activity or simply haven’t been able to find time for it lately, I encourage residents and visitors alike to grab a rod, head to the water, and make fishing an outdoor tradition.”

Outside of Free Fishing Days, Illinois requires anyone over the age of 16 to have a fishing license to fish.  At $15, Illinois has one of the most affordable standard fishing licenses in the Midwest.  Licenses can be purchased at vendors throughout Illinois or online.  Exclusions apply to active-duty military and people with disabilities.

title: COVER CROP FIELD DAY
full_story:
The Wayne County Soil and Water Conservation District is hosting a Cover Crop Field Day on Tuesday, August 18th at 4 pm at the Greg Dickey Farm in Wayne City.

Speakers will be David Kleinschmidt from Progressive Agronomy Consulting LLC,Torey Colburn from American Farmland Trust, and Dave Severin from the Illinois House of Representative.  There will be in field demonstrations, comparisons and a Soil Pit.

There will also be a meal for participants catered by Randy’s Smokehouse in Wayne City.  The Cover Crop Field Day is sponsored by the American Farmland Trust, Peoples National Bank and Farm Credit.

The Greg Dickey farm is located at 981 County Road 530, Wayne City, for more information call 618-842-7602 Ext 3.

title: ISA SEEKS CANDIDATES
full_story:
The Illinois Soybean Association is seeking candidates to fill an At-Large Director seat that recently became vacant.  Eligibility to serve requires candidates to be Illinois residents of legal voting age who share in the ownership and risk of growing and marketing soybeans.

Individuals will be nominated by the majority of Illinois Soybean Board (ISB) directors sitting in a quorum at a meeting to be determined.  Nominated individuals will be elected by a majority of soybean producers in attendance at the ISB Public Meeting on Wednesday, July 29th, in Champaign.  Illinois Soybean Board directors serve a term of three years and are eligible for up to three consecutive terms.

Any interested producer must notify the Board of their desire to become a candidate for an At-Large position by contacting Dustin Scott, Director of Operations, by July 17, 2026. Dustin can be reached at [email protected] or 309-846-3673.

Once intent is expressed, candidates will be emailed a link to an online application.  Online applications must be completed and submitted electronically no later than Friday, July 17th.  There is no write-in provision for At-Large Director elections.

title: CHRIS SIMPSON TO RETIRE
full_story:
The Illinois Eastern Community Colleges Board of Trustees has accepted the retirement notification of Chris Simpson, Vice Chancellor for Business Operations and President of Olney Central College, effective May 17th, 2027.

Simpson will conclude four years of service to Illinois Eastern Community Colleges, where he has provided leadership to both Olney Central College and district-wide business operations.  Since joining IECC in 2023, Simpson has helped guide the institution through the post-pandemic environment, supported implementation of the district’s one-college organizational model, and overseen key operational functions including business services, food services, and bookstore operations.

Prior to joining IECC, Simpson served as Superintendent of Richland County Community Unit School District No. 1 and brought extensive educational leadership experience to the college district.

As part of a planned succession strategy, the Board also appointed Ryan Hawkins as Vice Chancellor for Financial Operations and President-Designate of Olney Central College effective July 1st.

Hawkins currently serves as Chief Financial Officer for IECC and has been instrumental in the district’s financial planning, budgeting, facilities development, and long-range strategic initiatives.  Under the transition plan, Hawkins will continue to oversee district financial operations while spending the next year working alongside Simpson to learn campus operations and prepare to assume the presidency of Olney Central College upon Simpson’s retirement.

The year-long transition reflects the district’s commitment to leadership continuity and provides a unique opportunity for mentorship and knowledge transfer before the formal leadership change next spring.

The appointment also advances IECC’s ongoing efforts to align district-wide and campus-based business functions under a unified leadership structure, strengthening coordination and operational effectiveness across the institution.

Hawkins said he is honored by the Board’s confidence and grateful for the opportunity to work alongside Simpson during the transition period.

Simpson will continue serving as Vice Chancellor for Business Operations and President of Olney Central College through May 17th, 2027.  Hawkins will assume the presidency of Olney Central College and continue serving as Vice Chancellor for Financial Operations following Simpson’s retirement.

title: XENIA VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Xenia Village Board met in regular session last night.  The meeting started with the approval and swearing in of Terri Beckmen to fill the empty seat on the board following the appointment of Galen Garrison as mayor after the abrupt resignation of Dwight Casolari in April.

In public comments Alif Sherwani returned to give the board of trustees updates on the renovation of the village gas station.  Mr. Sherwani told trustees that the electronic computer system has been upgraded.  The next steps are to upgrade the pumps, followed by the awning and signage.

Mr. Sherwani also shared details of an incident of theft which took place and now involves the Clay County Sheriff’s office and the Illinois State Lottery Investigator.  Sherwani did not share any figures regarding the amount that was stolen.  He only remarked it was a “substantial amount.”  Sherwani once again requested the village approve a liquor license for the gas station.  Trustee’s decided to table the decision pending review of ordinances detailing the scope and powers of the villages Liquor Commissioner.

Brandon Bridges with Charleston Engineering provided Trustees with a joint funding agreement in the amount of $1,075,000 for the resurfacing of roads.  This covers 80% of the cost to resurface Church and Main Street.

Trustees discussed the state of properties in the village who have failed to comply with city ordinances.  The motion was made to send out one final notice before taking legal action.

Xenia Police Chief Jerry Burkett told trustees that he had attended two days of High risk stop and de-escalation training with the Mount Vernon Police Department.  Burkett also shared he took the police cruiser to the Gateway Way Speedway in Madison.

The Xenia Village board raised $5,430 dollars during the March 30 Ice cream social event.  Trustees also approved the Raffle license for the village Mud Bugs.

Village Superintendent Travis Lewis informed trustees that renovations on the villages lift station have been completed.

Finally, trustees discussed blocking the street for the Jaxson Green Benefit set for July 11th from noon to 5 pm with an auction to be held from 5 to 6pm.
